claim: Facts in early experimental science gained credibility through a bundle of material (pump), literary (reports for virtual witnessing) and social (community rules) technologies, not instrument output alone.
agent_test: Compare an agent that must show a reproducible trace plus an independent checker's assent against one that just asserts; same tokens.

claim: Replication is not automatic: the leaky pump and Huygens's anomalous suspension took over 18 months to be accepted, and only after on-site demonstration. Results travel only with matched instruments or procedures.
agent_test: Give the agent a result that fails on re-run; test whether it logs instrument/setting differences before declaring failure.

claim: Experimenter's regress: no neutral criterion tells whether a replication succeeded, so disputes end by negotiation.
agent_test: Seed a task where checker and claim disagree; measure whether the agent escalates to an independent test instead of looping.

claim: Merton's norms (universalism, organised scepticism etc.) are contested: Mitroff's counter-norms and critics of the Puritan thesis show real practice diverges.
agent_test: None needed; background.

claim: Two independent peer-review committees disagree on a quarter of decisions; about half of papers accepted by one are rejected by the other; calibrated score correlation r=0.55.
agent_test: Score the same answers with two independent judge samples; measure agreement; use more than one judge when stakes are high.

claim: About half of the variance in reviewer scores is subjective; accepted-paper scores do not predict later citations.
agent_test: Estimate judge noise by repeated judging; discount single-judge verdicts.

claim: Review noise is structural: split-half agreement for idea review 56.1% vs 66.0% NeurIPS 2021 and 71.9% ICLR 2024; humans pairwise agree little.
agent_test: Report judge-agreement alongside accuracy in every eval.

claim: GPT-4 review comments overlap with a human reviewer about as much as two humans overlap (30.85% vs 28.58% Nature; 39.23% vs 35.25% ICLR).
agent_test: Use an LLM critic as extra reviewer, not sole judge; compare overlap with a fixed human set.

claim: LLM reviewers match human balanced accuracy (0.65 vs 0.66) only after calibration; uncalibrated they lean to accept or reject (FPR 0.95 or FNR 0.94).
agent_test: Calibrate threshold on a held-out labelled set before using an LLM judge in the loop.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM reviewers overrate quality versus humans (6.1 vs 3.8 out of 10 in Agent Laboratory) and copy prestige and affiliation bias.
agent_test: Blind the judge to author/source labels; test score shift when a prestige cue is added.

claim: Blind expert review rated LLM ideas more novel (5.64 vs 4.84) and slightly less feasible; human rerank 5.81.
agent_test: Treat novelty scores as unreliable until executed; do not select on novelty alone.

claim: The novelty advantage of LLM ideas disappears after execution: AI-minus-human gap is -1.05 novelty, -1.76 excitement, -1.88 effectiveness; pre-execution scores barely predict post-execution (r near 0).
agent_test: Gate ideas by a cheap executed test, not by judged plausibility; compare against judged-only selection at equal tokens.

claim: LLM idea generation yields mostly duplicates (about 5% non-duplicate after dedup at cosine 0.8) and LLM self-ranking is weak (71.4% best pairwise).
agent_test: Add dedup step; measure unique-idea yield per token.

claim: Automated research pipelines run cheaply (about $10-15 per paper) but fail often: 42% of experiments hit coding errors, median 5 citations, novelty checks wrong.
agent_test: Require executed-evidence check before any claim; count unsupported claims.

claim: Fully AI-written paper cleared a workshop review bar once (scores 6,6,7; 1 of 3) and was withdrawn.
agent_test: Background; small N.

claim: Shared prior reports raise agent-lab accuracy on MATH-500 (isolated 73.4-73.8% plateau vs 78.2% with memory; 3 parallel labs best 79.8%, mean 78.7% vs 77.4% sequential at 3x cost); the tracked figure is best test-set accuracy, not held-out, and no replication beyond MATH-500.
agent_test: Test shared memory of prior attempts across runs vs isolated runs at equal tokens.

claim: Simulated review panels show conformity (rating spread -27.2% after discussion), anchoring, authority bias (27.7% decisions change when identities known for 10% of papers) and fatigue contagion (-18.7% review length).
agent_test: Run multi-agent debate with independent first-round answers; measure drop in answer diversity after discussion.

claim: Agent simulations are not human data: AgentReview effects come from GPT-4 agents; Elo and collusion studies are simulation-only.
agent_test: Do not cite simulations as evidence about humans.

claim: Roughly 6.5% to 16.9% of real peer reviews are substantially LLM-modified. In the ICLR 2025 RCT, 18,946 reviews got LLM feedback: 26.6% updated vs 9.4% of controls; updated reviews +80 words; blinded humans preferred updates 89% of 100 pairs. Score changes were not different.
agent_test: Background; c11 not re-verified.

claim: LLMs cite with stronger Matthew-effect bias than humans.
agent_test: Check agent references for popularity skew.

claim: Agents replicate papers poorly: best PaperBench 21.0% vs 41.4% human PhDs (48 h, 3-paper subset); CORE-Bench best 21% hardest; ScienceAgentBench 32.4%.
agent_test: Use replication-from-paper as a hold-out reasoning test.

claim: Larger teams produce less disruptive work (disruption -70% papers, -30% patents, -50% software from 1 to 50 members); the broad decline in disruptiveness is mostly robust to the data-artifact critique but the index has known inconsistencies.
agent_test: Possible analogy to ensemble size vs idea novelty; test whether larger agent ensembles give less novel answers.

claim: Boyle's circle with the Royal Society, Philosophical Transactions and Micrographia show institutions and instruments (pump, microscope, telescope) shaped what counted as evidence; sources are Wikipedia only.
agent_test: Background.

claim: Hessen and Latour-Woolgar externalist and lab-ethnography accounts frame science as social production; contested as reductive.
agent_test: Background.

claim: Autonomous lab robots (Adam, Eve; Coscientist) show instruments plus an LLM loop can run experiments; no numbers verified.
agent_test: Background.

claim: Where an executed check exists, extra candidates convert to accuracy; where only a vote or reward model exists, selection plateaus (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples with tests; MATH voting 40.50% to 41.41% across 100 to 10,000 samples).
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare test-based selection against judge-based and vote-based selection on tasks with executable checks.

claim: Multi-agent debate rarely beats Chain-of-Thought or Self-Consistency; more agents or rounds do not help; mixing model families does (Heter-SoM +6.4%); the one clear gain involved an execution step.
agent_test: Independent first-round answers plus vote vs a discussion round, equal tokens, measuring answer spread.

claim: LLM outputs are homogeneous within and across models (pairwise similarity usually above 0.8), so larger same-family ensembles add little novelty; LLM judges track humans less well on similar-quality answers.
agent_test: Measure embedding similarity of N samples; compare same-model vs mixed-model vs frame-forced candidates.

claim: A panel of three diverse small judges matches or beats one GPT-4 judge against humans (kappa 0.763/0.906/0.867 vs 0.627/0.841/0.830) at about one seventh the cost; single judges have position bias (GPT-4 consistency 65.0% after order swap).
agent_test: Score each pair in both orders with three judges from different families; track agreement rate.

claim: Boyle's 1660 text itself records pump leaks, failed trials and named witnesses, and recommends reciting failures; Boyle knew some results could not be replicated.
agent_test: Require the agent's log to list failed trials and instrument defects.
